newsitem.title: INDIA: TEXT-RBI statement on meeting with Chidambaram.
newsitem.headline: TEXT-RBI statement on meeting with Chidambaram.

text.p: Following is the text of a statement released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) after Finance Minister P. Chidambaram met RBI governor C. Rangarajan in the Indian capital:
"The post-budget meeting of the Central Board of the Reserve Bank of India with the Finance Minister was held in New Delhi today.

Finance Minister apprised the members of the Board that Governor, Reserve Bank of India, has been a great source of strength to the Finance Ministry. He further stated that the Governor's contribution in the present budget was immense and that the government was grateful for the wise counsel given by him.

Commenting on the Budget, the Finance Minister observed that 1996/97 had been a difficult year for prices because of lower wheat production and correction of administered prices which should have been done in previous year.
Finance Minister emphasised that price situation will be watched closely and imports of essential commodities made, if necessary.
Finance Minister said that price stability is critical since it is key to maintaining growth. Inflation should be contained at 6-7 percent as this would provide both economic and political stability.

Finance Minister felt that bank credit expansion is not taking place because of shyness of bankers, since the demand for credit very much exists. He urged that RBI must strongly encourage bankers to lend more actively. Some banks are willing to lend, others are not. Such slow growth of credit is simply unacceptable.
Finance Minister also urged that while there has been some softening of interest rates since October 1996, it is not enough and further reduction of lending rates would be desirable and possible.
The interest tax on banks has also been reduced. The minister suggested that the cost of banks' transactions needs to be reduced to facilitate softening of lending rates.

While welcoming the Finance Minister and the Minister of state, Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, Dr C. Rangarajan said that the recent budget for 1997/98 presented by P. Chidambaram three weeks ago has been framed not only in the context of today but of India as it should be at the dawn of 21st century. He hoped that all economic agents will respond adequately to the new initiatives in the budget so that a sustained growth rate of 7 percent can be achieved.
Dr Rangarajan expressed his satisfaction that the system of Ad hocs will be eliminated and replaced by a system of Ways and Means Advances. He highlighted the fundamental differences between the two.

The Ad hoc system was a permanent source of finance as the treasury Bills were rolled over whereas Ways and Means Advances is a temporary source of financing the mismatches between receipts and expenditure.
The new system, imparting greater fiscal discipline, will also enhance the autonomy of the Reserve Bank of India in the conduct of monetary policy and regulation of money supply.

Reiterating the objectives of monetary policy, governor clarified that the stance of monetary policy in the coming year will be two-fold as before. One is to regulate the money supply so as to keep the inflationary pressures under control and the second to provide adequate credit to support growth.

The regulation of money supply to keep the target level of 16 percent may have to contend in the coming year with large capital inflows. In this context it will be necessary to ensure that the reserve money expansion after taking into account net RBI credit to central government is consistent with the desired rate of monetary growth.

Despite reduction in CRR (cash reserve ratio) actual credit flow to commercial sector has remained low in the current year. Measures necessary to accelerate the flow of credit to support growth in output will merit attention."
